claims.statement: Remember people and past conversations; maintain professional relationships; support job searching/networking; track friends/family; all with categories/views.
Everyone, including friends and family.
100–500 and 500–2,000 people. Overlapping estimates, not a fixed count.
Professional background/roles/skills; personal details/family/interests; contact details/LinkedIn/websites; custom structured fields.
Company pages listing associated people; companies with notes and history.
In-person meetings/events; LinkedIn/social conversations; introductions/referrals/recommendations.
Date and a short sentence.
Profile; global quick-add; voice/dictation; ChatGPT or another agent.
One interaction can have multiple participants.
Elapsed-time suggestions; contextual follow-ups; a combination.
A separate People follow-up queue.
Typed colleague/friend/family/mentor/manager relationships; interactive graph; possible introduction paths. Who-introduced-whom tracking was not independently selected.
Profile links; one-time CSV/contact imports; periodic reimport with deduplication. No automatic profile sync or email/calendar interaction imports selected.
Directory/filters; timeline profile; follow-up dashboard; network; natural-language agent capture/querying; daily/weekly digest. Pre-meeting briefings not selected.
Public/professional information only plus private notes acceptable; proactive agent creation of records/reminders. Requires interpretation; not a settled field-level privacy policy.
Personal relationship information capture replaces loose notes; ordinary business meetings and action items are outside scope.
Separate facts from encounters so memory updates cannot fabricate last contact.
Generic organizations can cover schools and communities; the explicit company choice does not itself require a complete community-management system.
UI mockups guide layout and capture modes; all controls and fictional data remain proposals.
Task-backed follow-ups were suggested before the questionnaire but superseded by the selected separate People queue.
Automatic synchronization, email/calendar ingestion, and pre-meeting briefings were offered but not selected.
This run scopes the feature and does not authorize implementation, production migration, data collection, deployment, or scheduled messages.
First-release MCP must support discovery, read/search, creation, updates, fact append/correction, encounter logging/correction, and relevant organization/profile maintenance.

shape.appetite: Small capture-and-recall proof, then first release through imports/organizations/agent capture; reconnect and graph are follow-on milestones. No calendar estimate assumed.
shape.problem: Personal/professional information becomes loose notes; encounters and durable facts need distinct useful capture and retrieval.
shape.recommended_shape: Dedicated People records with optional note links; compact directory/profile/capture; shared UI/agent stores; first release m1–m3; richer m4–m5.

success_moves.move: Separate facts, encounters and direct-contact participation.
success_moves.benefit: Avoids fabricated recency from edits, imports and referrals about third parties.

success_moves.move: Prove capture with fictional fixture session before database wiring.
success_moves.benefit: Tests capture friction without risking the unresolved non-loopback data target.

success_moves.move: Reuse current main stores/MCP registry rather than rebuilding on old branch.
success_moves.benefit: Avoids duplicate foundations and narrows the new surface.

success_moves.move: Place imports after useful memory but before broad population.
success_moves.benefit: Limits duplicate and curated-data loss while preserving an early usable release.

success_moves.move: Use deterministic on-read suggestions before scheduling or generation.
success_moves.benefit: Makes snooze/dismiss rules testable without a background service.

success_moves.move: Record explicit relationships before rendering a bounded network.
success_moves.benefit: Prevents shared organizations or visual proximity from masquerading as acquaintance.

first_proof.question: Does short capture support useful recall without loose notes or fabricated last contact?
first_proof.artifact: Local fictional 25–50 profile capture page; then same flow on disposable PostgreSQL, with save/reload/search evidence.
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue when fact and shared encounter persist, facts leave contact unchanged, participants see one encounter, and detail search recovers context; proposed recall target 15 seconds. Simplify capture if friction defeats the loop.

simpler_counterproposal.proposal: Collection of person notes plus metadata and dated prose.
simpler_counterproposal.rejected_because: Reduces initial model work but makes source identity, shared encounters, fact/contact separation and reimport reconciliation awkward.
simpler_counterproposal.retained_simplification: Only four core models for first proof; device/agent dictation; no new recording/LLM/scheduler.

milestones.title: Capture a detail and recover it
milestones.outcome: Person/fact/shared encounter capture and retrieval, first in a deterministic fixture then persisted to disposable PostgreSQL.
milestones.proof: Fixture UI and focused rules; local database reload, shared participant recency, date correction/archive, failed save draft retention.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Small private capture/profile flow works; global navigation remains hidden until persistence passes.
milestones.rollback: Hide People routes; retain additive tables and records.

milestones.title: Use profiles across life contexts and agents
milestones.outcome: Directory, organizations, affiliations, contacts and complete first-release MCP discovery/read/search/write/update/append/log/correction access work over the same stores.
milestones.proof: Discover tools via MCP listing; find people without known IDs; fact search and paginated encounter reads; create profile/contact/affiliation, append fact, log shared encounter, read back, correct fact/encounter, archive/restore; assert unchanged unrelated fields and correct contact recency; verify each write family refuses read-only scope.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Small trial replaces loose notes; UI and MCP can discover, inspect, maintain, append, log and correct core People records; reconnect and relationship tools follow their later workflows.
milestones.rollback: Remove navigation/tool registration while retaining private records.

milestones.title: Populate and reimport without losing curation
milestones.outcome: CSV preview/apply/reimport and manual merge preserve canonical identity and curated fields.
milestones.proof: 500 rows twice, same-name/shared-contact collisions, curated edit, invalid row, partial retry, merge participant collision.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: First release supports curated and imported directory without silent overwrites.
milestones.rollback: Disable import/merge actions; preserve applied records and import outcomes.

milestones.title: Surface useful reasons to reconnect
milestones.outcome: Independent People queue and on-demand digest provide sourced reasons with persistent snooze/dismiss/resolve.
milestones.proof: Fixed clock, duplicate generation, unknown contact, opt-in, snooze, dismissal, archive/merge, no TaskItem creation.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Useful quiet reconnect surface exists without scheduling or external delivery.
milestones.rollback: Hide reconnect/digest commands; retain memory workflow and suggestion state.

milestones.title: Explore known relationships and possible introductions
milestones.outcome: Explicit typed edges support focused network and source-backed possible paths.
milestones.proof: Directed/symmetric edges, false employer-only path, cycles, archives, self root; browser pan/zoom/list accessibility.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Relationship entry remains useful independently of the graph.
milestones.rollback: Hide graph/path lookup; preserve profile relationships and first-release workflow.
